name: The Briefing Room
lesson: Controls, the hypothesis-driven hunt loop, and the Pyramid of Pain.
pivot_tip: Start broad on the 'name' field, then narrow with 'host' or 'parent'.

e001.title: The Hunt Loop
lines: THREAT HUNTING IS A LOOP, NOT A CHECKLIST
1. HYPOTHESIZE   Start from a testable idea: 'An adversary is using PowerShell
launched by Office documents on finance workstations.'
2. HUNT          Query telemetry to prove or disprove it. Filter, then pivot on
what you find (host, user, parent process, domain, hash).
3. INVESTIGATE   Collect evidence, build a timeline, map behavior to ATT&CK.
4. RESPOND       Contain and eradicate in the right ORDER. Too early tips off
the adversary; too late lets them spread.
5. IMPROVE       Turn every finding into a detection so it never surprises you again.
Incident response follows NIST SP 800-61: Preparation -> Detection & Analysis ->
Containment, Eradication & Recovery -> Post-Incident Activity.
e001.tip: A good hypothesis is specific enough that a query can prove it wrong.

e002.title: The Pyramid of Pain
lines: /\        TTPs (tactics, techniques, procedures)   TOUGH!
/  \       Tools                                    Challenging
/    \      Network / host artifacts                 Annoying
/      \     Domain names                             Simple
/        \    IP addresses                             Easy
/__________\   Hash values                              Trivial
The higher you detect, the more it costs the adversary to change.
A new hash takes seconds. A new IP takes minutes. A new domain, an hour.
But changing HOW they operate (their TTPs) means retooling and retraining.
Hunt for behavior, not just indicators.
e002.tip: Blocking a hash is easy for you and trivial for them to dodge. Detecting a behavior hurts.

e003.title: Intel: VELVET LOCUST profile
lines: ADVERSARY PROFILE: VELVET LOCUST (fictional)
Motivation : Data theft and extortion against engineering firms
Known TTPs : Invoice-themed phishing with macro documents,
encoded PowerShell, scheduled-task persistence,
LSASS credential theft, SMB lateral movement,
HTTPS beaconing with DNS fallback, double extortion
(steal data first, then threaten encryption).
Dwell time : Hours to days. Moves fast once it has credentials.
Halcyon Dynamics crown jewels: the finance ledger on VAULT-DB-01.
e003.tip: Intel tells you what to hunt for. Telemetry tells you whether it happened here.

objectives.title: Check in with Oracle
objectives.desc: Walk up to Oracle and press E.
hints: Oracle is the glowing hologram near where you started.
Walk next to Oracle until the [E] prompt appears.
Stand next to Oracle and press E (or click Oracle).

objectives.title: Study the training rig
objectives.desc: Investigate TRAIN-01 and read both artifacts on it.
hints: Nodes glow until you investigate them. Look for TRAIN-01.
Stand next to TRAIN-01, press E, and open each artifact.
Open both 'The Hunt Loop' and 'The Pyramid of Pain'.

objectives.title: Open your Evidence Journal
objectives.desc: Press J. Everything you collect is saved there with timestamps.
hints: The journal key is J.
You can also click JOURNAL on the toolbar at the bottom.
Press J now.

objectives.title: Run your first hunt
objectives.desc: Press T to open the Hunt Terminal and type: search proc where name="notepad.exe"
objectives.success: One row, exactly what you asked for. That's filtering.
hints: Press T, type the query exactly as shown, and press Enter.
Quotes matter: name="notepad.exe".
search proc where name="notepad.exe"

objectives.title: The Pyramid of Pain
objectives.desc: Press B to open the Hypothesis Board and answer Oracle's question.
objectives.prompt: Which indicator costs an adversary the MOST to change once you detect it?

options.feedback: Bottom of the pyramid. Recompile once and the hash is new.
Cheap to change. They rent a new server in minutes.
Annoying for them, but a new domain costs an hour and a few dollars.
Top of the pyramid. Detect behavior and they have to change how they work.

hints: Re-read 'The Pyramid of Pain' in your journal.
The top of the pyramid is labelled TOUGH.
TTPs.

objectives.title: Open the ATT&CK Matrix
objectives.desc: Press M. You'll light up cells here as you map what VELVET LOCUST does.
hints: The matrix key is M.
Or click MATRIX on the toolbar.
Press M.

objectives.title: Know your adversary
objectives.desc: Read the VELVET LOCUST profile on the Threat Intel Wall.
hints: The intel wall is another node in this room.
Find INTEL-WALL and press E.
Open 'Intel: VELVET LOCUST profile'.
